error_codes.name: Upstream dependency timeout
error_codes.notes: Root-cause pattern. An upstream DAG or feed did not complete in time, so the downstream job either fails outright or proceeds on stale/partial data and fails later for a different-looking reason.

error_codes.name: EMR executor OutOfMemoryError
signature_phrases: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits
error_codes.notes: Symptom pattern. Executor ran out of memory. Can be a standalone data-volume issue, or a downstream symptom of an upstream timeout that caused the job to run on a larger-than-normal or malformed partition.

error_codes.name: Input file / path not found
error_codes.notes: The job's expected input path or partition was not written by the upstream process, or was written to the wrong location.

error_codes.name: S3 access denied
error_codes.notes: The pipeline's own EMR role could not read or write the S3 object it needed. Distinct from a tooling-level access-denied on the agent's own log-fetch call -- this is the DAG's own read/write failing, present inside the log text.

error_codes.name: Generic DAG task failure
error_codes.notes: Catch-all pattern with no more specific signature present. Lowest precedence -- if a more specific error code also matches, prefer the more specific one.

precedence_rules: When more than one error_code's signature phrases are found in the same log, the error_code with the LOWER precedence_rank number wins (rank 1 = root cause, highest priority; rank 5 = generic catch-all, lowest priority).

Known co-occurrence: UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_003 (rank 1) commonly appears earlier in the log and causes a downstream EMR_OOM_002 (rank 2) as the job proceeds on stale or oversized partitions. When both signatures appear in the same log, classify as UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_003, not EMR_OOM_002.

If the only phrases present are generic (DAG_TASK_FAIL_004) with no more specific signature, and no other error_code's phrases are present, DAG_TASK_FAIL_004 is the match, but confidence should be scored lower to reflect the lack of a specific root cause.

If two error codes of similar specificity (not a known root-cause/symptom pair) appear with comparable strength and no precedence rule disambiguates them, do not force a match -- score confidence below the 0.95 floor and let the escalation rule apply.
